newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba Oil earnings rise on cost-cutting.
newsitem.headline: Veba Oil earnings rise on cost-cutting.

text.p: Group net profits at Veba Oil, a unit of German diversified utility Veba AG, grew nearly 70 percent to 354 million marks ($204.6 million) in 1996 on the back of cost savings, the group said on Tuesday.

The group also benefited from a firmer dollar over the year, management board chairman Wilhelm Bonse-Geuking said, although group sales were hit slightly by lower prices in the petrochemical industry.
He forecast higher earnings for the current year.
Sales net of mineral oil tax grew to 18 percent to 12.1 billion marks in 1996 from 10.1 billion marks the previous year, Bonse-Geuking said.
The firmer dollar and higher prices affected the oil and natural gas sectors, but the advantages from this were hit by higher costs for raw materials in the petrochemical area and lower turnover.

Chief financial officer Bernhard Winzinger said around half of sales hike was due to higher prices, five percent came from the firmer dollar and the remaining four percent came from increased turnover.
The group said the proposed introduction of a mineral oil tax was "contraproductive in every way," Bonse-Geuking said.
A tax increase of 20 pfennigs per litre would be the fourth such a tax increase in seven years and would mean an increase in petrol prices of 110 percent since 1990.

The group said that it had still not resolved problems at its Aral petrol-station chain. Earlier this year, Veba denied speculation it was in discussions to buy U.S. oil giant Mobil Corp's stake in Aral.
Mobil holds around 30 percent of Aral, a situation which Veba views as unsatisfactory.

While Veba holds a dominant 56 percent stake in Aral, Mobil Oil is on the supervisory board and Veba has said previously that it fears that British Petroleum Co Plc will have access to important strategic information through its partnership with Mobil.
The speculation arose in the wake of the downstream link-up between Mobil and BP in February last year.
Bonse-Geuking said that the most important consideration was that Aral's leadership in the German petrol-station market was not threatened.
Veba Oil said that it planned to cut a further 300 jobs in the current year, after cutting 400 jobs last year. The group employed 5,300 people at the end of 1996. ($ = 1.730 German Marks)
